cohort: The study included 24,256 pregnant women admitted to Kasturba Maternity Hospital in a tribal area of Gujarat, India, between 2016 and 2021, who were screened for sickle cell disease.
finding: Pregnant women with sickle cell disease had significantly higher risks of maternal death, anemia, severe anemia, preterm delivery, cesarean section, stillbirth, and low birth weight compared to those with normal pregnancies, with risks highest during the last month of pregnancy.
mod_finding: Women with SCD pregnancy had a higher risk of cesarean section (AOR 5.5, 95% CI: 4.7-7.0) compared to normal pregnancies.
